newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traffic normal, strikes loom at French airline.
newsitem.headline: Traffic normal, strikes loom at French airline.

text.p: Air France Europe flights operated normally on Wednesday morning but the threat of new strikes hung over the state-owned airline after talks between ground staff unions and management broke down, the airline said.
An airline spokeswoman said a strike by pilots had ended and the airline was not cancelling any flights.
But she did not rule out traffic disruption after ground staff unions meet at 10 a.m. (0800 GMT) at Paris' Orly airport to discuss their next step.
Unions complained their minimum demands were not being met and accused management of dragging its feet.
After heavy traffic disruption at the weekend, Air France Europe cancelled all flights from Orly on Tuesday morning, restoring normal services later after negotiations began.
Unions protest against the unifying of Air France Europe's more generous pay and employment terms with those of parent company Air France AIRF.PA.

The stoppage highlighted labour disputes dogging French airlines on the day that Air France took a key step towards a full merger with the former Air Inter, set for September, leasing the domestic carrier's activities and staff.
Management says terms need to be brought more into line with those of lower-cost competitors such as British Airways as deregulation takes effect on European Union domestic routes.
